_comment: Single-core control for the conc64_gemm label in tools/run_multicard_sweep.sh.
conc64_gemm runs the whole of workloads/basic/tensor_gemm_ops/gemm.json with one
worker per logical core, 64 of them pulling from a shared queue. Every reported
latency there is still a single-core latency, so the concurrency loss is the diff
against one core of the same instance -- but running the same 648 cases serially
on one core is around 3h of wall time (they take 192s of measurement at 64-way,
and the work does not shrink), against a 4h watchdog, and a run the watchdog kills
writes no report at all.
So the control is a subset, chosen to be exactly the shapes the 64-core run is
read at:
* M=1 is the latency floor, where the answer is launch overhead and not the
array, so 64 concurrent workers ought to hurt it most if the host is the
bottleneck;
* M=512 is the transition, M=4096/20480/28672 span the compute-bound plateau,
and 28672x4096x4096 is where bf16 peaks at 64 cores (147.9 TFLOPS, 88.7% MFU);
* K.N is the two square shapes rather than all four -- the skewed ones move the
peak by <2% at 64 cores, so they do not change the ratio.
float8 is one shape per format on purpose: 16384x8192x8192 is the slowest case at
64 cores by two orders of magnitude (458ms, 1.5% MFU), and 192 vCPUs shared 64 ways
was the obvious suspect for it -- which only a single-core number can rule out.
Compare per case, not peak-to-peak: ONLY=conc1_gemm here vs conc64_gemm there.
